verdict.rationale: The Trusted Agent Protocol spec documents an HTTP 402 path. When a merchant answers with a 402, the agent's signed Agentic Payment Container carries a payment IOU, and the merchant can grant access after verifying it, with funds expected at settlement. This is a first-party rail for checkout-less agent payment, but it is a single thin mention in the spec. Missing for 10: per-call pricing/metering guidance for monetizing an API, documented settlement and IOU-redemption flow, developer integration examples or SDK support for the 402 flow, hands-on or independent corroboration, and production maturity (the product is still 'in the process of development and deployment').

support.subject: As a developer, I can monetize an API or service with HTTP 402 machine payments that agents pay per call without a checkout UI

citations.quote: when a merchant requests payment with an HTTP 402 response code, "a payment IOU will be present"; after verifying it, "the Merchant can grant access with the expectation that the funds will be available when settlement occurs."
Signatures carry a tag of "agent-browser-auth" or "agent-payer-auth" per interaction
